utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The affirmation you made to tell the truth still applies. Mr. Popovic is finishing his questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Pantelic.

utterances.speaker: MILOS PANTELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Pantelic, before we begin and continue with the documents, I'm talking about page 12057 of the transcript, lines 12 to 15. This is your testimony on Friday. So just for the sake of clarification, I will ask you to answer a few questions that I have. First of all, did you receive daily bulletins or reports which talked about events from the public security department and related to the previous day?

utterances.speaker: MILOS PANTELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mostly received these bulletins regularly, sometimes it would happen that one would cover the previous two days, depending on the obligations of the analysis department of the Ministry of the Interior. However, I can say that I received them regularly for a number of years.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did these bulletins mention anti-terrorist operations being conducted in the territory of Kosovo and Metohija? Was it mentioned in any way?

utterances.speaker: MILOS PANTELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The daily bulletins included events, important security events, from the territory of Kosovo and Metohija and the terrorist actions were briefly described in a few sentences. As for the taking of anti-terrorist measures or activities, that was not included in the daily reports. The staff in Pristina was in charge of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Pantelic. As far as I remember, that was precisely what you said on Friday, however, something else is recorded in the transcript and this is why I had these questions for you. Now I would like to continue where we left off on Friday.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please see D434, which is your tab 18, Mr. Pantelic. Yes, that's just the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Pantelic, this is the summary from the meeting of the minister with the chiefs of secretariat held on the 16th of October, 1998 in Belgrade, and it was drawn up by the analysis administration. Can you tell us what sort of meeting this was?

utterances.speaker: MILOS PANTELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These were meetings held periodically, roughly every three months. There were five meetings a year at the most, and we discussed the results of the work during the previous period, mostly the quarterly period. The main problems within the Ministry of the Interior were examined, all problems from the remit of work of the Ministry of the Interior, some conclusions were drawn, and on the basis of the conclusions, certain measures were ordered. The meeting was attended primarily by the minister who chaired the meetings and also assistant ministers, chiefs of administrations from the seat of the Ministry of the Interior and chiefs of territorial organisational units, that is to say, chiefs of the secretariats of the interior.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please see page 3 of this document in both versions. And if you could please focus on paragraph 3. That's just the page.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: And it says, minister of Internal Affairs, Mr. Vlajko Stojiljkovic, said that the purpose of the meeting was to analyse the results of work in the several months of the year and to determine the tasks for the remaining months of the year. Can you just comment on that?

utterances.speaker: MILOS PANTELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The meeting was usually opened by the minister of the interior, but he was not in charge of chairing the meeting. It was usually a chief of the sector or one of the assistant ministers from the seat of the Ministry of the Interior. Most of the times it was one of the assistant ministers. So a meeting would be opened by the minister, he would also deliver the final presentation, and he would say what the conclusions were, but the meeting was chaired by one of his assistants.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please see page 8 in the B/C/S version. That is to say, page 6 in the English version. Yes, that's the right page.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: And will ask you to have a look at paragraph 3 once again, Mr. Pantelic. The sentence that says: "In this year." Have you managed to find it?

utterances.speaker: MILOS PANTELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On page 8 paragraph 3 is not that sentence.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Not page 8. It's page 5. It's not page 8 of the document. This is what the heading says in B/C/S. If this is easier. And the third paragraph a sentence that says: "In this year." Have you managed to find it?

utterances.speaker: MILOS PANTELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you please read it for yourself, maybe this paragraph as well as the following one and tell us what this is all about. Also, tell us whether that was the information presented at this meeting in connection with events in the territory of the Autonomous Province of Kosovo and Metohija.

utterances.speaker: MILOS PANTELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I just said that at the meetings of this kind, terrorist activities of Albanian separatists were presented. That was just brief information totalling several sentences. It was mentioned what the number of these actions was, how many of people on their side were wounded or killed during these actions, that is to say, what were the consequences of that kind of conduct on part of the Albanian separatists. However, at the meeting with the chiefs of administrations and chiefs of secretariats, we did not examine any detailed information. It is mostly important to say that anti-terrorist actions were also not mentioned and were never discussed.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please have a look at page 12 in the B/C/S version, which is page 11 in the English version. And on top of the page it is page 10 in the document you have in front of you, Mr. Pantelic.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: If you see under (b), primary tasks of the public security department this year, I suppose. It's not very legible. Can you just have a look at what the tasks are as they are listed under item 1. Could you tell us if these were regular tasks that fell within the remit of the public security department of the Serbian MUP?

utterances.speaker: MILOS PANTELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These were certainly regular tasks that fall within the remit of the Ministry of the Interior, that is to say, the territorial organisational units of the ministry. But after the discussion at the meeting once the overall security situation was examined, it was agreed what should be done in the coming period. The primary actions, as they are formulated here, can be found in any minutes from these kinds of meetings. The priority was usually given to crime, that is to say, detecting and suppressing crimes that fell within regular crime and economic crime. Also preventive measures aimed at the suppression of both these kinds of crime, that was the main purpose of the work of this ministry. In addition to that, there was a lot of talk about keeping law and order, which is the basic task of the ministry, to protect the lives and property of citizens. There were also problems with crossing the state border, the conduct in the border zone, other administrative tasks, weapons, travel documents, and so on and so forth. There were also problems connected with fire-fighting, with activating territorial firefighter units, as well as activities connected to traffic inspection, as well as logistical services within the ministry. Therefore, that was the subject of these meetings, that was what the conclusions related to, and on the basis of these conclusions, relevant measures were ordered.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please see P1204, which is your tab 19.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: That is dispatch number 36. The date is the 25th of November, 1998. First of all, is it meant to be sent to the whole territory of the Republic of Serbia?

utterances.speaker: MILOS PANTELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the usual, the so-called holiday dispatch, and it was addressed to all organisational units that come within the remit of the Ministry of the Interior, and it orders stepped-up security measures, activities, in the coming holiday season. At the end, it also say that is it should be addressed to the information analysis administration and that that should be an aggregate report on the security situation during the same holiday, so this was a regular dispatch, it was regularly sent during the holiday seasons, and it ordered the carrying out of special security measures.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please see D436 now.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: That is your tab 20. That is dispatch number 2323. The date is the 11th of December, 1998, Mr. Pantelic, and the question for you is whether this was addressed to everyone in the territory of the Republic of Serbia. Can you please also look at paragraph 2 and tell us what are the subjects discussed in this dispatch?

utterances.speaker: MILOS PANTELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This dispatch talks about the action Valuta. It is an action that was established in the 1990s. As far as I remember in 1991 or 1992 in Serbia we had huge inflation. The value of the dinar was falling and at the time this action was established in order to suppress illegal buying and selling of foreign currency of all kinds, so all kinds of selling, reselling, and buying of foreign currency. Later on once the foreign exchange rate with the dinar was settled, then this kind of activity stagnated, and in this situation when we expected that circumstances would be extraordinary due to political pressure against Serbia, there was also a lack of staple foods and fuels and other things necessary for the normal life of any citizen, this problem became rife once again. Therefore, this dispatch was sent by the chief of the public security sector, and he ordered that special measures be taken. I wouldn't talk about that in more detail because I think everything is described here in detail.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MILOS PANTELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And let me also answer your question, the second paragraph says here that per the order of the minister and with the name at energetic and efficient prevention of these incidents, it is necessary to engage the required number of operative workers. This is precisely what we did in practice.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now, if we can please see the Exhibit Number P356. This is your tab 22. Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: This is dispatch number 312 dated 18th of February, 1999. Could you please first of all tell me whether this was a dispatch intended for everybody in the territory of the Republic of Serbia, and then I will ask you question by question because I want to focus on the contents of this dispatch which is rather lengthy.

utterances.speaker: MILOS PANTELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is rather lengthy dispatch, and it regarded all the organisational units of the Ministry of the Interior included the secretariats of the interior.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Pantelic, if you look at paragraph 2 of this dispatch, at the end of this paragraph, you can see that it was necessary to undertake the following measures, and these measures then included a list of measures 1 to 20. In order to avoid going through all of them, could you please take a look at these measures and then briefly explain whether these included the measures that fell within the remit of public security sector and in which way were these measures supposed to be carried out?

utterances.speaker: MILOS PANTELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What was ordered by this dispatch all falls within the regular operations of the public security sector or all of its organisational units. In this paragraph under item 1, it is ordered to update the defence plan focusing on the plan of stand-by measures, mobilisation plan, and plan of preparing for defence. This included, first of all, an update of the establishment list of both active and reserve forces. The number of active forces was well known and last time we already talked about the ways in which reserve forces could be engaged, and it was only the minister that was in charge of this, or a person authorised by the minister by his decision. In this dispatch, it was ordered to activate, update, control, and man such units because in the meantime, it happened that certain persons fell ill, some of them due to their psychological condition were unable to carry out certain tasks, so it was the task of the department in charge of police within the secretariat and some of the inspectors who worked within this department to update these plans and to update them on a daily basis. So certain measures were not supposed to be ordered for anybody who carried out their tasks regularly and appropriately. From what I could see now very quickly, apart from the establishment of reserve command posts, the plans that regarded people's defence and securing special reserves for secretariats and police units in their locations, also prohibition of going abroad, prohibition of taking leave and so on, so these are all regular activities apart from those activities that fall under the remit of people's defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. We will not go through all of the items, there are many of them, but I believe that you are acquainted with all of them. The only thing I would like to learn more about, if you would please take a look at item 6. And if you could provide us with a brief comment.

utterances.speaker: MILOS PANTELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This item 6 was topical even earlier. This was a very difficult period, the borders were closed, we were exposed to sanctions, and there was a general lack of staple foods and energy sources, and these were very pronounced problems. For this reason, it was ordered that we had to plan to increase beat duty and control all the facilities and also that we had to undertake certain actions for perpetrators of criminal activities.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would now like to see Exhibit D438. This is your tab 23.

utterances.speaker: MILOS PANTELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a dispatch that was sent to all the secretariats of the interior. It was sent on 2nd of March, 1999. At that time when we could already guess that the Rambouillet negotiations would not yield any results, then in earlier dispatches it was ordered that the management had to organise duty operations in different organisational units. This lasted for a substantial period of time, so they were already exhausted, and they could not carry out their regular duties, their regular tasks in an adequate manner. Bearing this in mind, this dispatch was sent from the Ministry of the Interior so that the management could, in a way, be relieved for a while and obviously this would impact very much their regular duties.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. We can see here at the top of this dispatch that it says: Regarding dispatch number 312 of 18 February 1999. So is this the dispatch that you commented a short while ago which served as a basis for this one?

utterances.speaker: MILOS PANTELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This dispatch is actually just a continuation of what was ordered previously.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. But now that we are talking about this, could we please go back to page 356. This is the previous dispatch that you could see dated the 18th of February. When we spoke about that dispatch, could you please take a look at item 7 on page 2 in B/C/S, possibly page 3 in English. Item 7 which reads: "Through more intensive operational work and undertaking of other measures, make appropriate controls over paramilitary units and their members." Could you please tell me what was the meaning of this item 7? What was your reading of this, and what did you do as a result of this item 7?

utterances.speaker: MILOS PANTELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the explanation may be a very simple one. The Law on the Interior prohibited the ministry from engaging other units apart from members of the reserve forces of the ministry. So when this item 7 says that through intensified intelligence and other measures and actions, they were supposed to carry out the necessary checks and establish complete control over volunteer and paramilitary units and their members, what is meant here is that members of the Ministry of the Interior were obliged, each of them in their respective territory, to list such occurrences, inform the relevant military commands about this, and send such people to military departments that had territorial jurisdiction so that they could proceed in line with the relevant legislation at the period.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Just to be a bit more precise, Mr. Pantelic, you are talking about both volunteers and paramilitary units, are you?

utterances.speaker: MILOS PANTELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As regards paramilitary units, I never had any of them in my territory, and we never registered any such occurrence. As regards volunteers, I also can't remember that we had many of those, so they were probably organised in a different way in the territories or in the territories of municipalities which did not fall under my remit, under the remit of my secretariat.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please tell me, the Law on People's Defence that you mentioned, which category it regulated, the volunteers or paramilitary formations?

utterances.speaker: MILOS PANTELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that the Law on People's Defence did not regular [as interpreted] paramilitary units. Usually these were people who came from the ranks of criminals, and we tried in every way we could to eliminate their partaking in any kind of volunteer units.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Could we now please have a look at Exhibit P716.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: It is your tab 24. Mr. Pantelic, this is dispatch number 544 dated 16th of March, 1999. First of all, was it intended for everybody in the territory of the Republic of Serbia and whether this dispatch talks about regular tasks falling within the remit of the public security sector, and if you could very briefly comment on this dispatch?

utterances.speaker: MILOS PANTELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This dispatch talks about the situation. I can't even see here who signed it. But it describes the situation when in the municipalities that were -- within the jurisdiction of different secretariats, we had a large number of immigrants, refugees, and different other persons who did not have their residence, not even temporary residence in the territory of the Republic of Serbia. So this dispatch orders certain measures to be undertaken by the organs of the Ministry of the Interior in order to resolve this problem in an adequate manner. That is, in order to register all the persons who were present in the territory without being properly registered, without their residence being properly registered. For this reason, the IT department of the ministry provided lists of all the citizens and their addresses, so streets and house numbers, so whoever had their residences registered, and on the basis of this, one part of the uniformed police officers worked in relevant sectors that they were charged with to carry out certain checks in order to update the registers and as it is stated here, next to names of persons they had to put certain signs in order to make sure that we can identify these persons.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Pantelic, for the reasons of our transcript, given that we do not have your answer recorded in the way in which you said it on page 12, line 5 to 6, I would kindly ask you to repeat your answer to this question. So my question was, whether the Law on the Defence regulated the issue of volunteers or paramilitary units and you answered, so could you please repeat this answer because the transcript does not reflect what you actually said.

utterances.speaker: MILOS PANTELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I said, as for volunteers, that was one situation, and paramilitary units were something quite different. Volunteers were directed to go to certain places that were determined by the Law on All People's Defence and that were under the jurisdiction of military territorial organs. As for paramilitary formations, on the other hand, I had none of them in my sector, and I did not send any reports relating to them to the Ministry of the Interior. However, I do know because that followed from some earlier dispatches that such formations were to be suppressed in every possible way, and they were not to be allowed to join the regular forces of the Ministry of Defence because they usually originated from the ranks of criminals.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. It was only for purposes of clarification. You have told me everything in connection with the document P716, which is signed by Mr. Vlastimir Djordjevic. It is not easy to read on the last page. I'm just interested in knowing whether this dispatch once again covered tasks and duties that come within the regular remit of duties of the public security sector?

utterances.speaker: MILOS PANTELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, absolutely. These are regular tasks that fall within the responsibilities of the public security sector, but the tasks that special attention needs to be paid to are emphasised therein.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Could we now please have P1206 on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: It is your tab 25. Very briefly this is dispatch number 597. It is not easy to see the date, but it's the month of March 1999. It says the 22nd of March in the translation into English. I will only ask you to comment briefly on this, who was this dispatch addressed to and what it is about.

utterances.speaker: MILOS PANTELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This dispatch was intended to all organisational units of the Ministry of the Interior, and it ties in with the dispatches that we just commented on. It just orders stepped-up measures, and the emphasis is on the danger that terrorists actions might be launched in the territory of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now please see D237.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: It is your tab 26. This is a dispatch dated the 24th of March, 1999. We can see that it was sent by the minister Vlajko Stojiljkovic, and it is a decision to take special measures under the jurisdiction of the government of the Republic of Serbia in view of the declaration of a state of imminent threat of war. Can you please tell us whether this covers the entire territory of Serbia and tell us briefly what this dispatch is about, and you might also focus on item 2 of the decision.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Could you also indicate, Mr. Popovic, the exhibit number of the previous dispatch, 597, of the 22nd of March.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, the number of the exhibit is P1206.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You are welcome.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Pantelic, please go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MILOS PANTELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a dispatch addressed to all chiefs of secretariats and other heads of organisational units within the MUP. It was sent on the 24th of March which was the day on which the NATO aggression against the FRY began. In this dispatch, the minister wished to inform his men about the decision on the implementation of special measures under the jurisdiction of the government of the Republic of Serbia, in view of the declaration of a state of imminent threat of war. In addition to the Ministry of the Interior, measures are ordered also to all other organs and organisations belonging to the state administration as well as various companies and so on. What is interesting here is that we should focus our activities on preparing the units to perform duties relating to resisting the enemy attacks against our country, so particularly these are combat duties and that was what the Ministry of the Interior was supposed to do as its primary task. However, it is also mentioned that specific security measures still need to be taken and that the emphasis should also be on the suppression of racketeering, black-market, all other types of illegal conduct, that the shortage of staple foods should be prevented and all other obligations are listed as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: I'm just reading the transcript, and once again it seems that something is missing, so just to clarify. Can you please tell me, when you said this, did you mention something like the military Ministry of the Interior, is there such a term at all? Are you talking about the Ministry of the Interior here and the tasks that the Ministry of the Interior had?

utterances.speaker: MILOS PANTELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is a no such thing as a military Ministry of the Interior. There are territorial military organs which have territorial responsibilities and jurisdictions, and I was talking about them.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: All right. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please see Exhibit 65 ter 1809, please. Your Honours, if you will I allow this and if my colleagues from OTP have no objection, this is a document that was not listed on the Defence 65 ter list, but we submitted it to the OTP, and we notified them in a timely fashion, so I would use it now while questioning this witness, and it is just another dispatch.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The document may already be an exhibit. P1139.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If that is so, it will make the whole situation easier, but this is not the information I had and that is why --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Carry on, Mr. Popovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: All right. Mr. Pantelic, it is your tab 27. The 25th of March, 1999. It is a dispatch submitted by the minister of the interior, Mr. Vlajko Stojiljkovic. Can you please read it and tell us if it covered the entire territory of the Republic of Serbia, and then I will have several questions for you in connection with this dispatch.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: There seems to be some difficulty about the document on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The document is 65 ter 1809 from the 65 ter list. Or I could give you the number D011-3563. Yes, that is the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Pantelic, let me repeat the question. Was this dispatch sent all over the Republic of Serbia?

utterances.speaker: MILOS PANTELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It was intended for all secretariats of the interior in the territory of the Republic of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: All right. The dispatch is signed by the minister of the interior Vlajko Stojiljkovic. Can you please have a look at the second sentence which says: "You have received orders from me personally on how to proceed." I'm listening, please answer.

utterances.speaker: MILOS PANTELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this dispatch relates to everything that was ordered earlier, whether by the minister or by the chief of the crime suppression department or the chief of the public security sector. It has to do with numerous speculations, crimes, and prohibited conduct of persons and taking of certain measures is required here. What is interesting in this dispatch is that regardless of the difficult situation in connection with the supply of staple foods at the time, especially bread, was the request that within one hour a report is to be sent to the ministry. That was practically impossible at the time. It also says that if such cases should occur in the future, arrest the persons without a judge and detain them in custody to await my decision. The Law on Criminal Procedure was in force at the time and the decree on the implementation of the law on criminal procedure during a time of war had not yet come into force. As far as I remember, it came into force only in early April or thereabouts. Therefore, such conduct, arresting persons without the judge and detaining them in custody until the minister's decision, would be a criminal offence according to the law that was in force at the time. The last paragraph in the dispatch is also irritating. It says that if we permit such occurrences that we will suffer the same consequences. We who had spent our careers in police, and we commented on this, were very much irritated by this sort of attitude of the minister to us. We did not express that openly, but dissatisfaction was evident.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Pantelic, now that we are talking about the minister personally, tell us, what were the relations like within the Ministry of the Interior, and was it usual for the minister to send dispatches such as this one?

utterances.speaker: MILOS PANTELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me answer the second part of your question first. I never received a dispatch like this. I have spent many years in the public security sector, but I never received such a dispatch, nor would I ever implement it in practice. As for the relations within the ministry, the Ministry of the Interior, many things have changed in the last few years, practically since 1997 when Minister Stojiljkovic was appointed the head of the ministry. During my work in the ministry I remember that there were five different ministers, and none of them ever worked in this way. Practically he had taken on himself much more than he could actually carry. He had appointed assistant ministers from various lines of work. These were four assistants, and each of them was in charge of certain lines of work within the ministry. He also had the chief of service who was behind all this, that was happening with the assistants. He withheld many of the jurisdictions that the chief of service previously had, and all that caused much problems within the Ministry of the Interior. This was not reflected a lot on the work of the secretariat of the interior because we were responsible only to the chief of the public security service. However, relations were disturbed in terms of lines of work.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Just to clarify some of what you mentioned in your answer. Firstly, for the transcript, can you tell us something more about the role of the chief of the public security service because I think your answer was not reflected in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MILOS PANTELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I have to talk about the earlier period when Mr. Sokolovic was the minister, that was the period before the year 1997. At the time he had chief of the service who was at the same time assistant minister of the interior. He was elected by the parliament of the Republic of Serbia to be the minister. He was a politician, and he left the work to professionals. So at the time the chief of the public security service had full responsibility, assistant ministers as such did not exist, chiefs of administrations at the seat of the ministry reported for their work to the chief of the service, and the minister was in charge of conducting politics of representing the minister of the interior with the government and the Assembly of the Republic of Serbia to security the funds and proper conditions for the work of the ministry. But as for the professional duties of the members of the ministry, he left that segment of work to professionals to perform. So they were the ones who were in charge of the work, who established what was to be done. Of course, with the co-ordination of the minister, with his full inspection and supervision. However, in this case everything was turned upside-down. Minister Vlajko Stojiljkovic took all the authority on him. He meddled in the work of the lines of work within the ministry as well as the work of secretariats as territorial organisational units. I can claim that even though I rarely saw him, I believe only two or three times during his term in office, that even then we had conflicts because we could not understand each other when it came to resolving certain personnel problems, but also professional security problems.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Pantelic, but if I could refer you back to my question and the role of the chief of the public security sector starting from the moment when Mr. Stojiljkovic became minister of the Ministry of the Interior. And also what you said concerning this in your previous question [as interpreted], so what was his role once he was appointed minister, and you can immediately tell us where do you get this information, what is the source of your information?

utterances.speaker: MILOS PANTELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that I already answered a substantial portion of your question. The relationships within the ministry were the topic of our conversations. I went to the ministry at least once a week and on those occasions I visited chiefs of all the administrations within the Ministry of the Interior. I spoke to them, we made certain arrangements. Obviously I had to be given some directions concerning my future work. I had to be informed concerning the overall security situation. And on those occasions during the unofficial exchanges, there were quite a few comments concerning the method of work of the then-ministry [as interpreted], and this is something that chiefs of all the administrations were familiar with because many of them had significant problems. He had his own point of view concerning these problems. He came from the world of politics, from the world of the economy. He used to be chairman of the Chamber of Commerce. He now came to a state administration body, and he had to find his way. It would have been appropriate if he allowed the professionals to carry on their tasks, rather than to take all the authority upon himself, which is something that he did. During the war operations of NATO, I also went to the chief of the sector and chiefs of other administrations including Dragan Ilic who was head of the crime suppression administration, and I was present in his office, I believe it was on Topcider hill, this is where his war office was, and within half an hour the minister called him -- or within half an hour the minister called him three times and issued orders concerning certain tasks. Something similar was experienced by other chiefs within the secretariat, so when we met and talked to one another and when we had some conversations aside from our official tasks, in a way we came to an agreement that the things within the ministry were not functioning as they were supposed to.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you tell me at that time what was the function of Mr. Draganic?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: Dragan Ilic.

utterances.speaker: MILOS PANTELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Dragan Ilic was chief of the administration of crime police. In 1997, assistant ministers were appointed at the level of the ministry, so apart from the chief of public security sector, there were three additional assistant ministers. Each of them was in charge of a single line of work. Regardless of the fact that there were chiefs of administrations at the level of the ministry who were directly responsible for their work to the chief of the public security sector, the first of them was Radomir Markovic who was responsible for criminal police work, and in addition, for analysis and information analysis, although there were already chiefs in charge of this within the sector. When he became chief of state security sector, he was not controlled through a particular line, so to say, so when he was chief of administration of criminal police, he was directly linked to the minister, and he received tasks directly from the minister.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would just kindly ask you for the needs of the transcript on page 21, line 22. It should state minister rather than ministry. This follows from the logic of this answer, so I would not ask the witness to repeat this answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Pantelic, in relation to this dispatch which was the basis for your answer, if you look at the very top of this document, it says: Valjevo SUP, then 10 and some letters and 23:16. Can you see this number?

utterances.speaker: MILOS PANTELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is hardly legible but, yes, I can see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: In one part of your answer you said that you never received this dispatch, so could you please explain what was this all about and what does this Valjevo SUP actually mean?

utterances.speaker: MILOS PANTELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't believe that I said that I did not receive this dispatch. I never stated this. This dispatch was sent to everybody. And what was written here, Valjevo SUP, I can recognise my own handwriting, so this dispatch was sent, among other secretariats, also to the secretariat of the interior of Valjevo, but I did not forward it because I found it absurd, and this is why I wrote down here that it had to be archived.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Well, I believe this was entered into transcript a bit differently, so we've now clarified this. My next question for you is the following: Was the minister personally ever present at the collegium meetings that you held at your secretariat, so would he come to the secretariats, was he in touch with the chiefs and people who were subordinated to you?

utterances.speaker: MILOS PANTELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The minister very rarely visited secretariats. He would visit them in certain situations if some personnel had to be replaced, or, for example, if the territory of one of the secretariats was visited by some disasters or if some accidents occurred there. Given that during the war operations Valjevo was bombed by NATO on 21 occasions and the only building of the secretariat of the interior in central Serbia, apart from the territory of the Autonomous Province of Kosovo that was hit was that one, it was hit by NATO projectiles on two occasions, and for this reason we moved out to our war location. There were no casualties, but he felt the need to come visit our secretariat and see the conditions in which we operated. Chief of the public security sector, Mr. Djordjevic, came with the minister and also the assistant minister and head of the general affairs administration, Mr. Zekovic. This meeting that they were present at the minister and chiefs of the ministry was held in a small room at our war location and from the territory of the secretariat of the interior, we had there chiefs of departments of the interior and also chiefs of the internal organisational units within municipalities. I opened that meeting, and the chiefs of organisational units reported about the security problems each of them concerning their own remit. I can't remember many details, but I do believe that neither the chief of the public security sector nor the chief of general affairs administration uttered anything during this meeting. After my final word, that is, after the reports that we received from the chiefs of organisational units and after my conclusions, the minister directly ordered what was it that we were supposed to do in the following period in which way and within which time-limits we were supposed to do that. During that meeting, I also got the impression that he took it upon himself -- that he took all the authorities of the chiefs of organisational units upon himself, so all the organisational units that belonged to the Ministry of the Interior.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Pantelic.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If we now see Exhibit D238. I apologise, before we do that, I would kindly ask for the previous document, I would kindly tender it into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit D00784.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If we could now see the Exhibit D238 on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: This is your tab 28, Mr. Pantelic. I believe it is dated 25th of March, 1999. If you could very briefly tell us whether this dispatch was intended for the entire territory of the Republic of Serbia, whether these are the ordinary tasks that fall within remit of the public security sector, and who signed this dispatch, and whether this was usual occurrence for the minister to issue this kind of dispatch which is, again, related to everything you stated earlier?

utterances.speaker: MILOS PANTELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a dispatch that as far as I can see was sent on the 25th of March, so the aggression was already well underway, and the federal government order certain measures to the ministries, and the minister of the interior also ordered us certain things that we had to undertake in those particular circumstances. I would not like to spend too much time on these points. This dispatch was sent by the minister, but even before we undertook similar measures, so basically this dispatch had no additional meaning for us.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Pantelic.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If we could now please see on the screen the Exhibit Number D440. I apologise -- no, this is your tab number 30. We will later come to your tab 29.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Pantelic, the date here is March the 27th, 1999. Dispatch number 1352. Once again I would like to know whether this was intended for the entire territory of the Republic of Serbia, if you could briefly comment on the fact that this dispatch was sent by assistant to the minister, major General Stojan Misic.

utterances.speaker: MILOS PANTELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As you've said, this dispatch was sent on the 27th of March and it regards the government decision to proclaim the state of war and the order to carry out various preparation measures. It is related to updating of lists of foreigners with permanent residence and issuing of passports to soldiers during their military service, military conscripts and professional soldiers. In the situation of the kind after the NATO aggression was initiated many people tried to avoid their military service in one way or the other. For that reason, this dispatch was sent out by assistant to the minister Stojan Misic, who was in charge of border-related tasks, administrative tasks, foreigners and so on, also liaison and so on. Later on he was also in charge of analysis, information analysis, fire-fighting and so on. So these are the tasks that fell under his remit.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now if we could see the Exhibit D255.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: This is your tab 29, dated 26th of March, 1999. Once again if you could tell us whether it was intended for the entire territory of the Republic of Serbia, what was this dispatch all about, and if you could comment briefly on who signed it. We can see here that this was Major-General Dragan Ilic, chief of administration.

utterances.speaker: MILOS PANTELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this dispatch was also sent on the 26th of March to all the secretariats, and it ordered measures that were previously ordered, who knows how many times, so in any way we were supposed to prevent the prices of staple foods from increasing creation of unnecessary reserves. We usually talked about flour, oil, energy sources and so on. So as chief of administration, he could write such a dispatch because he was in charge of these tasks, so the topic here was to prevent crime, which was one of the tasks within his remit.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now please see the Exhibit D253.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: This is your tab 31. This is a dispatch from the chief of public security department number 1353 of the 27th of March, 1999. And it has to do with the finding of missile-guiding device, the so-called locators. Once again I will ask to you tell us whether this was intended for the entire territory of the Republic of Serbia, and we can see under paragraph 3 that members of the traffic police are mentioned, so did this fit in with the description of the regular tasks and duties of the public security department? Could we just hear a brief comment from you?

utterances.speaker: MILOS PANTELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This dispatch was also addressed to everyone. It is a so-called circular dispatch as we called it. It had do with attempts to find the so-called locators that were placed close to important facilities and roads. It is described here in detail how they are to be identified, how they can be de-activated, and it is also mentioned that those from the ministry who were in charge of that should be informed about that. As for the members of the traffic police, that they will conduct searches of the main roads and more important regional roads, this was just logical because they performed their regular tasks and duties on such roads or there somewhere in the vicinity, and they are always able do something in connection with this dispatch. So these were their regular tasks and duties.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please see D257 now.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: It is your tab 32. This is a dispatch dated the 6th of April 1999. And my question for you is whether this was also intended for the entire territory of the Republic of Serbia, and if you look at paragraph 1 it is a decree on the implementation of the Law on Criminal Procedure during the state of war, and there is a signature chief of administration, Major-General Dragan Ilic. What is your comment on this dispatch?

utterances.speaker: MILOS PANTELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Rather than dwell on certain provisions of this dispatch, let me say that the organs of the Ministry of the Interior were given somewhat extended authority in comparison to the authority that they had according to the Law on Criminal Procedure that was in force. In the decree, which the government of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia adopted, it says that the decree on the implementation of the Law on Criminal Procedure shall only be used in situations when this is not contrary to the implementation of the Law on Criminal Procedure. So the organs of the interior are given certain authorities to carry out certain investigation activities without the presence of a prosecutor so that they can begin the preliminary investigative procedure, but they were obliged to inform a prosecutor post festum but very urgently about all that. They could also remand someone in custody up to 30 days. I mean, the organs of the interior, though the maximum of time to keep someone in custody was up to three days according to the Law on Criminal Procedure at the time. So there were other prerogatives as well. For instance, those relating to arresting persons, opening letters, and so on and so forth.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I wish to move to another subject, and I think it's time for the break now, so if you agree this might be a proper moment for the first break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, we'll have the first break, and we will resume at 4.15.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Popovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Pantelic, before we continue with exhibits, I will ask you to clarify some of the answers you have given in connection with page 20, line 7. I think that this was not properly recorded. You were talking about the period when Mr. Sokolovic was the minister, and just to clarify this, can you tell me who was the chief of the public security sector, and what additional duty did he have?

utterances.speaker: MILOS PANTELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The chief of the public security sector was at the same time the deputy minister of the interior.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And one more thing that I wish to clarify with you, it is on page 23 in lines 5 to 9. Mr. Pantelic, here you talked about the moment when Mr. Radomir Markovic became chief of the state security sector and the fact that Mr. Ilic had his own line of work at the time and what sort of relation he had with the minister. So if you could please repeat from the moment when Radomir Markovic became the chief of the public security sector, what was the rank had by Mr. Ilic, and what were his relations with Minister Vlajko Stojiljkovic.

utterances.speaker: MILOS PANTELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that earlier at the moment when Radomir Markovic became chief of the state security sector, the chief of administration, Dragan Ilic, did not have any line control by the responsible assistant minister. He was independent, and he was attached to the minister in a way.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Your answer is recorded in one way, and you answered in different way again. Can you please repeat the last sentence. He was independent and what did you also say, let me not repeat that.

utterances.speaker: MILOS PANTELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was independent, that means he did not have a line control by the assistant minister, so he was directly connected with the Ministry of the Interior as the chief of administration.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: It is all right now, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please see Exhibit P1050.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Pantelic, it is your tab 33. This is the dispatch. The number is 2571, dated the 9th of April, 1999. My question for you is whether it was intended for the entire territory of the Republic of Serbia, and we'll see in paragraph 1 that that is the same paragraph 2 that what is regulated here are work relations and -- just a second, please. For the third time we have an answer to the same question, so I have to ask the Trial Chamber for their allowance for page 31, line 18. Once again, it's not what the witness said. Can you repeat once again what was it about Dragan Ilic, who was he directly subordinated to?

utterances.speaker: MILOS PANTELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me repeat again. Dragan Ilic, as the chief of the crime police administration, was directly subordinated to the minister of the interior.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Let us now return to the Exhibit 1050. It is the decree on regulating employment relations and disciplinary responsibility. Can you please look at the first part and briefly comment on that and then later I will ask you to comment on other parts of this dispatch, but we'll do it piecemeal because it's a longish document.

utterances.speaker: MILOS PANTELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says at the beginning that a decree on Internal Affairs during a state of war was published in the "Official Gazette." It came into effect on the following day and that was why the dispatch was sent. What was the difference between the specific situation ordered here and the previous situation in which the discipline of employees was regulated in detail, both in the Law on Internal Affairs and on the decree of the government on the disciplinary responsibility of employees of the Ministry of the Interior? This Law on Decree regulated the matter in detail. However, now we were in a situation that during the state of war a decree on Internal Affairs during the state of war was adopted, and it regulated in detail the disciplinary proceedings. The difference was that the disciplinary proceedings were shortened as much as possible and that in this case when there were more serious violations of duty only the chief of the secretariat was responsible. Previously there would be first a preliminary proceedings which meant that the immediate superior, if it was established that someone might have breached discipline, would first take the statement of such a person, then file a report, then submit the report to the chief of the secretariat, and the chief of secretariat, if he believed that there was a basis for that, he would then submit it to the disciplinary prosecutor who would, together with the disciplinary investigator, would conduct the entire proceedings, and eventually the problem would be judged by a disciplinary court. There was also a second instance, and in the second instance, the higher disciplinary court within the Ministry of the Interior was responsible. However, by this decree it was allowed to the chief of secretariat who was firstly authorised by the chief of the sector of the minister of the interior could make decisions even in cases of serious violations of duty without the disciplinary proceedings in the typical sense of the word, that is to say, without the disciplinary investigator and disciplinary court.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. That was just an answer to what I wanted to present to you, so I will ask you to confirm that.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If we could please see the next page of this document now.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: After items 1 and 2, that's maybe the fifth paragraph from the top in B/C/S where it says: "The chief of the department of public security has authorised the heads of organisational units to impose prescribed measures and sentences for serious violations of employment obligations and duties." Was that what you just told us?

utterances.speaker: MILOS PANTELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is precisely that. The chief of the department of public security in accordance with this decree authorised the heads, that is to say, the chiefs of territorial organisational units, that is to say, the secretariats, and together with this dispatch, the written authorisation should have been submitted as well, allowing them to conduct disciplinary proceedings in accordance with this decree. And of course they were allowed to impose penalties.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you also please look at the bottom of the page in Serbian. It is the last sentence which begins by the words: "The implementation of the said decree implies the change of procedure in first instance because a disciplinary penalty and penalty for a serious violation of obligations and duties shall be made by the head of the organisational unit at the proposal of the immediate superior." Could you please previously comment on that.

utterances.speaker: MILOS PANTELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If a direct superior learns that there was a breach of discipline, whether it was minor or major breach of discipline, he should first interview the employee, take a statement, then also interview the witnesses of the incident, and submit a report to the chief of secretariat. The chief of secretariat, by authorisation of the chief of the public security sector, will then make the relevant decision and impose a disciplinary penalty.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Pantelic. Let us just try to connect this with a specific situation on the ground in connection with the Special Police units which you sent to the territory of Kosovo and Metohija. Was this an information that you would receive as the head of an organisational unit?

utterances.speaker: MILOS PANTELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, certainly. We were informed even earlier. For example, we could see what it looked like if a member of a Special Police Unit who was sent to carry out special security tasks in the territory of Kosovo and Metohija committed a breach of discipline. In that case, his immediate superior under whose command he is at the time, it could be chief of department or it could be a chief of a police station, whoever it was at the moment he noticed such a breach of discipline, he would initiate the proceedings and even though he was in the territory of Kosovo and Metohija, he would then submit a disciplinary report to the chief of the secretariat who was territorially in jurisdiction for sending this Special Police unit to the territory of the Autonomous Province of Kosovo and Metohija.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now please see D259. It is your tab 34.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Pantelic, this is dispatch dated 9 of April 1999. My question is whether this was intended for the entire territory of the Republic of Serbia. If you look at this, you can see that it refers to a large number of decrees. Could you tell us who sent this dispatch?

utterances.speaker: MILOS PANTELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This dispatch was sent to all the secretariats of the interior. It was sent by assistant minister Stojan Misic, and it refers to decrees that the Ministry of the Interior had to abide by. The government of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia ever since the beginning of the state of war and thereafter adopted about 15 such decrees. And only four of them fell within the remit of the Ministry of the Interior. One of them was the decree on the Internal Affairs during a state of war. Then we had the decree on gathering of citizens, decree on residence, and decree on personal identification papers during a state of war. Not much changed after these decrees were adopted, but what needs to be said is the decree on gathering of citizens during a state of war prescribed that public meetings could be held only upon issuing of an approval by the territorial competent body. Before that it was sufficient to apply for such a permit. The decree on residence of citizens regulated that all persons older than 14 years of age had to register their residence or temporary residence within the shortest possible period of time. And finally the decree on personal identification documents during the state of war also reduced the age limit for issuing of an ID from 18 to 14 years of age, so these were the regulations that stemmed out from the decree of the government and that fell within the remit of the Ministry of the Interior.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And finally, who sent this dispatch?

utterances.speaker: MILOS PANTELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I said earlier, it was sent by the assistant minister, Mr. Stojan Misic.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now see the Exhibit Number D260, please, on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: This is your tab 36. This is a dispatch dated 11th of April, 1999. I would like to know whether it was intended for the entire territory of the Republic of Serbia, who sent it, and we can see that the goal here was a single handling, single method of handling of humanitarian aid consignments.

utterances.speaker: MILOS PANTELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, in order to avoid any abuse concerning the deliveries of humanitarian aid and earlier, different security organs noted that there were occurrences of this kind. For this reason we received this dispatch, and also the federal government adopted a decree which regulated this particular issue. So at a session of federal government, the federal ministry for health care and social policy was designated as the body that needed to co-ordinate these tasks. Also it was determined that it was the Yugoslav Red Cross organisation which was supposed to receive such consignments. So the goal was here to prevent any mishandling or abuse, and this dispatch regulated uniform handling of consignments in the entire territory of the Republic of Serbia. I don't believe that it is necessary to go through all of these measures because I think it's self-evident.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now see the Exhibit Number P1207.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Pantelic, this is your tab 37. I would kindly ask you now to tell us once again whether this was intended for the entire territory of the Republic of Serbia. In the last sentence of first paragraph we can see that in addition to measures sorted earlier, the following must be done. Given that there aren't this many measures listed here, could you please read them in order to be able to provide us with a brief explanation, and could you please tell us whether these measures fell under regular remit of the public security sector, and this dispatch was signed by Mr. Djordjevic.

utterances.speaker: MILOS PANTELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This dispatch was sent to everybody, and these are certainly regular tasks of the members of the public security sector. Item 1 calls for co-operation with town and municipal civilian protection staffs in order to organise members of hunting, marksmen, scouting, mountaineering, and other organisations in order to be able to find locators which we described a short while ago. So we had to engage all the other forces within the society in an attempt to prevent the damage by NATO attacks to the facilities in the Republic of Serbia. Item 2 says that with district chiefs and other subjects in charge of implementing the spring sowing plan, we were supposed to take control over oil derivatives and artificial fertilisers and similar. This is something that we did immediately prior to this state of war and later on. And thirdly, we were asked to prevent any kind of black-marketing activities. This is something that we already discussed here today, and we could see at least four dispatches concerning this particular subject matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please see Exhibit Number D261. This is your tab 38.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: This is a dispatch dated 19th of April, 1999. My question is as follows: Was it intended for the entire territory of the Republic of Serbia? Could you tell us in briefly what it is all about, and if you could please focus your attention on item 2, which says that the increased migration of citizens leaving Kosovo and Metohija for places outside this area has been noticed and that they submitted requests to register their residents, and this dispatch was sent by Mr. Stojan Misic, assistant minister.

utterances.speaker: MILOS PANTELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This dispatch was sent on the 19th of April to everybody. It was sent by the assistant to the minister, Mr. Stojan Misic, who was in charge of this particular line of work. Ever since the NATO aggression was initiated against the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia we noticed very extensive migration because bombing of the territory of Kosovo and Metohija occurred daily, and the consequences were very harsh. In such a situation many Serbs fled to the territory of the Republic of Serbia. This created certain problems related with their registration. So registration of their temporary residence or their residence, their addresses and everything else. And this dispatch was sent precisely for that reason.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please see the Exhibit D262.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Pantelic, this is dispatch dated 21st of April, 1999. My question is whether it was intended for the entire territory of the Republic of Serbia, this dispatch was sent by General-Major Zekovic, assistant to the minister. And in paragraph 1 it says: "We provide you with explanations concerning the decree on Internal Affairs during the state of war." You talked about this when we saw one of the previous dispatches, so could you please take a look at this one and see what it's all about and then confirm if this follows the same line that you described earlier.

utterances.speaker: MILOS PANTELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this dispatch simply precis the provisions of the decree on Internal Affairs during a state of war. Here the disciplinary proceedings are regulated in detail, disciplinary proceedings against members of the Ministry of the Interior. I think I explained a short while ago how these proceedings were to be initiated, who could file reports, disciplinary reports, whom to, and so on. So this is simply a more precise explanation of what was already stipulated by the decree on Internal Affairs during the state of war.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now please see the Exhibit D407.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: This is your tab number 40. Mr. Pantelic, the document dated 23rd of April, 1999 says: "Daily review of current events and occurrences regarding public security for 22nd of April 1999." Before we start reviewing this document and before you receive my question concerning this document, could you tell us in which forms of information existed and in which way were the information conveyed in 1998 and 1999 within the public security sector of the Ministry of the Interior?

utterances.speaker: MILOS PANTELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were three types of reporting. First of all, urgent reporting, daily reporting, and periodical reporting. These types of reporting were based on an instruction on reporting that was developed by the Ministry of the Interior, and that instruction also included a list of current security events that the ministry was supposed to be informed about. When it comes to urgent reporting, it was carried out in line with that list, which listed with precision all the security events that had to be reported urgently to the ministry by telephone. As a chief of the secretariat, I also had to report concerning such events to certain political structures in the territory in which my secretariat was. When it comes to daily reporting, it was also regulated by the previously mentioned instruction. Daily reporting went from the lowest possible organisational unit of my secretariat, that is from the department of the interior at the level of municipalities, through the departments and sections at the seat of the secretariat and the person in charge of the duty shift collected the information on the current events for the previous day, for the previous period from zero hundred hours to 2400 hours. Such information were then conveyed by the chief or head of the duty shift to the administration for analysis of the Ministry of the Interior. So priority were received by the operational centre of the ministry and then forwarded to the analysis administration. And there again in line with that instruction on reporting and information certain analysis were carried out, and on the basis of received information, they would come up with this kind of daily review of current events and occurrences related to public security. And then from the analysis administration in Belgrade, this kind of daily review was submitted to all the secretariats of the interior so that they could have an overall picture concerning the public security situation in the entire territory of the Republic of Serbia. This was not a confidential document. As you can see it is not classified, and it was submitted to all the territorial organisational units. And at the seat of the ministry, the chief of sector could decide who such daily review would be submitted to. The third type of reporting was periodical reporting, so these were monthly reports or quarterly reports, and annual reports. Although in the meantime, if we had a particular problem we had to follow it by a special report. So the monthly reports obviously regarded the public security situation for a given month for the entire territory of the Republic of Serbia, and this was rather similar to this daily review, apart from the fact that they were more comprehensive, and particular accent was placed on some lines of work.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now take a look in more detail concerning this particular exhibit. So this is daily review of current events and occurrences relating to public security for 22nd of April, 1999. We can see that the date of this dispatch is April the 23rd, so it concerns the events that occurred on the previous day.

utterances.speaker: MILOS PANTELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Here on page 1 we can see characteristic events and occurrences and then in paragraph 1 we can see on 21st of April, 1999, using six or eight projectiles, refugee colony of Meja was hit.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Before we proceed, I would kindly ask the following page to be shown in both languages where we can see on the 24th of April, near the village Zagradska Hoca near Prizren, and here it says that there was a terrorist attack and that in this attack a member of the reserved forces was killed. My question for you is: Are anti-terrorist activities or operations mentioned anywhere in this daily review, anti-terrorist operations that took place in the territory of Kosovo and Metohija?

utterances.speaker: MILOS PANTELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These reports never mentioned anti-terrorist operations. But terrorist operations conducted by the Albanian separatists were mentioned. This review only briefly described in two or three sentences what happened, in which area and what the occasion was. Hundreds of such reports have passed through my hands, and they never mentioned which measures were taken by the members of the public security in the territory of the Autonomous Province of Kosovo and Metohija in order to deal with certain situations.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Let us just look at page 3 of this document as well. We'll see in the first paragraph that the secretariat in Kragujevac is mentioned, that it arrested a certain person and remanded him in custody, and the next one is the secretariat in Smederevo and so on. My question for you is the following: Did this daily report apply all events that fell within the regular activities of the public security sector in the entire territory of the Republic of Serbia?

utterances.speaker: MILOS PANTELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These were certainly the regular activities of the members of the minister of the interior in the territory of the entire Republic of Serbia. In accordance with the instructions on reporting, on the basis of which this daily report was drawn up, a selection of the more important security incidents or events was made, so this is the basis on which it was made.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Could we please see D408 now.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: It is tab 41 in your binder, Mr. Pantelic. This is a dispatch number 1290 dated the 24th of April, 1999. Once again, it is a daily review of characteristic events and occurrences in the public security area for the point throughout April 1999. The question is the same. Does this document anywhere mention anti-terrorist actions or actions carried out by the units which were stationed in the territory of Kosovo and Metohija? Please have a look at the document.

utterances.speaker: MILOS PANTELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This report again mentions terrorist attacks on members of the police on two or three occasions or four, as many as are listed here. However, no anti-terrorist activities are mentioned as far as I can see.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Pantelic. Once again just for the sake of transcript on page 44 in line 3, when we talk about these documents, these are daily reviews of current events and occurrences, these are the reports of the public security sector, right?

utterances.speaker: MILOS PANTELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, certainly.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please see -- but, no, while we are looking at this document, D408, if we could see page 3 in both versions.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Please have a look at that. It says that there were 65 traffic accidents in which three persons lost their lives and 16 were lightly or seriously injured. Once again my question is: Were these regular duties of the police from the entire territory of the Republic of Serbia?

utterances.speaker: MILOS PANTELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I do not need to answer the question because the title says daily review of current events and occurrences from the area of the public security for that date. So these were the regular duties of the members of the Ministry of the Interior.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Pantelic. Will you please now have a look at the Exhibit D409, which is your tab 42. If you can just briefly in two sentences comment on that. It is another daily review of current events and occurrences for the 25th of April.

utterances.speaker: MILOS PANTELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All of these dispatches look like one another, so in this dispatch, just like in the previous ones, we can see that it was sent to all heads of territorial organisational units in the territory of the Republic of Serbia, and it lists the current security events which took place during the previous day. Let me not move from one to the other. It is a fact that there are several events here which are in connection with the terrorist activities of the Albanian separatists in Kosovo, and like in the other dispatches, there are also problems relating to public law and order, protection of personal property and security of citizens, then control of traffic, control of border crossings, implementation of the Law on Fire-arms, and so on and so forth. So that was the overview of all current security problems.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please have a look at D411.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Once again just a very brief comment. It is your tab 44. And it is a daily review of current events and occurrences dated the 27th of April, 1999.

utterances.speaker: MILOS PANTELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is nothing special I would have to add to everything I just said earlier. It all applies to this review of current events and occurrences. Some terrorist actions in the territory of the Autonomous Province of Kosovo are mentioned as well as some serious crimes committed in the territory of the Republic of Serbia on the previous day.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Pantelic, I could show you one or two documents like these, but in order to save time you have seen several of these daily reports now. My question for you is this: In any of the daily reports, which you received as the chief of secretariat, did you ever see any mention of any anti-terrorist operations that were being conducted in the territory of Kosovo and Metohija during the year 1998 and 1999?

utterances.speaker: MILOS PANTELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Such anti-terrorist operations were not mentioned in these daily reports for the simple reason that they did not fit with the instruction on reporting which the Ministry of the Interior submitted to us. The instructions only mentioned terrorist activities, but not the measures that were taken. So we did not have any information about that or received them through these reports. At least, I do not remember that it was so.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Pantelic.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please see Exhibit P1208.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: And it is your tab 46. Mr. Pantelic, this is dispatch number 206 dated the 29th of April, 1999. SUP to everyone, 1 to 33, to the chief, and it was signed by the chief of public security department Colonel-General Vlastimir Djordjevic.
